claims.text: The untreated cast refractory high-entropy alloy has a coarse-grained, single-phase BCC microstructure.
The untreated alloy has high strength and high impact-induced energy release but limited ductility.
Solution treatment at approximately 1600°C for 1 hour followed by rapid quenching will homogenize the alloy.
Cold rolling to approximately 50% reduction will promote grain subdivision.
Aging at approximately 800°C for 4 hours will precipitate a fine dispersion of coherent carbides or nitrides.
The proposed treatment will produce an ultrafine-grained microstructure.
The proposed treatment will produce a uniformly dispersed population of fine, coherent precipitates.
Grain refinement increases the density of high-angle grain boundaries.
A higher density of high-angle grain boundaries slows crack propagation.
Grain refinement and high-angle grain boundaries improve strain accommodation.
Coherent precipitates provide precipitation strengthening that preserves high yield strength.
The refined grains and coherent precipitates together promote more uniform deformation during impact.
The refined grains and coherent precipitates preserve the alloy's impact-induced energetic performance.
The treated alloy will have greater elongation to fracture than the untreated baseline.
The treated alloy will exhibit more uniform deformation under impact loading than the untreated baseline.
Yield strength and impact-induced energy release will each decline by no more than approximately 10% after treatment.
Keeping the processing parameters within the stated ranges will avoid phase instability and over-aging.

The hypothesis is falsified if elongation does not improve significantly by more than approximately 15–20%, or if yield strength or impact-induced energy release decreases by more than approximately 10%.

contradictions.description: The route is called a two-step treatment, but the intervention describes three principal processing stages: solution treatment/quenching, plastic deformation, and aging.
